steps.title: The Math of the Rubik's Cube
Area Under a Curve: Accumulation & Integrals

lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.goal: See how one math idea looks as a picture, in words, and as an equation.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.start: Pick your grade level at the top, then open any station to try 5 guided questions.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.prerequisite: Start at any grade that feels comfortable — you can switch levels anytime.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.check: Show the same problem with a drawing, an equation, and a one-sentence explanation.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.goal: Count objects, compare groups, and connect adding and subtracting to real stories.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.start: Build a group with counters, then test your answer on the Operations station.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.prerequisite: Counting out loud and comparing which group has more.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.check: Tell a short story for your addition or subtraction equation.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.goal: Spot what repeats or grows in a sequence and explain the rule in plain words.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.start: Look at the first few terms on the Patterns station and predict what comes next.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.prerequisite: Counting and noticing shapes or numbers that repeat.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.check: State the rule that takes you from one step to the next.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.goal: Use ones, tens, and hundreds blocks to estimate, regroup, and check multi-digit math.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.start: Inspect the base-ten blocks on the Place Value station before typing your answer.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.check: Explain what each digit in your answer is worth.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.goal: Connect equal groups and dot arrays to multiplication and division facts.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.start: Count the rows and columns in the array model before computing.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.check: Write both a multiplication fact and a matching division fact for one array.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.goal: Understand fractions as equal parts of a whole and points on a number line.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.start: Count how many equal parts make the whole, then how many are shaded.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.prerequisite: Equal sharing and division into groups.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.check: Explain what the top number (numerator) and bottom number (denominator) tell you.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.goal: Measure sides, angles, perimeter, and area by counting units instead of guessing formulas.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.start: Use the grid and measurement model on the Geometry station to test your idea.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.prerequisite: Measuring length and multiplying side lengths.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.check: Explain the difference between distance around the outside and space inside.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.goal: Read tables and bar charts carefully and spot what the data actually shows.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.start: Compare the bar heights and axis scale on the Data station.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.check: Write one true conclusion supported by the chart.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.goal: Work with positive and negative numbers using temperature, elevation, and a number line.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.start: Locate zero on the number line first, then track direction and distance.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.prerequisite: Adding, subtracting, and ordering numbers on a number line.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.check: Explain why subtracting a negative number moves you to the right.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.goal: Keep both sides of an equation balanced while solving for an unknown value.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.start: Picture a balance scale: whatever you do to one side, do to the other.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.prerequisite: Order of operations and signed numbers.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.check: Plug your solution back into the starting equation to prove both sides match.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.goal: Connect input-output tables, rules, and graphs to see how one quantity changes with another.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.start: Test two inputs in the function machine to spot the steady rate of change.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.prerequisite: Solving equations and recognizing number patterns.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/math-fou.check: Show how the rule in words matches the numbers in the table.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/numbers..goal: See how humans went from tally marks to place value, primes, fractions, and binary.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/numbers..start: Try the number-system playground to build the same quantity in different ways.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/numbers..check: Why does place value (and zero) make big calculations so much easier than tally marks?

lessons/mathematics/foundations/clocks-a.goal: Read analog and digital clocks and calculate how much time has passed.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/clocks-a.start: Move the hour and minute hands on the interactive clock and predict the time.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/clocks-a.prerequisite: Counting by fives and reading a number line.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/clocks-a.check: Explain how you count minutes from one time to another.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/measurin.goal: Pick the right measurement unit for any scale, from tiny atoms to galaxies.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/measurin.start: Slide across the cosmic scale explorer and compare two objects side by side.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/measurin.prerequisite: Comparing lengths and reading a ruler.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/measurin.check: Which unit fits your chosen object best, and why?

lessons/mathematics/algebra/unit-factory.goal: See how changing the unit changes the number without changing the real amount.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/unit-factory.start: Pull the conveyor lever to turn weights into different units, then test a conversion.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/unit-factory.check: When 1 kilogram becomes 1,000 grams, what stayed the same and what changed?

lessons/mathematics/foundations/multipli.goal: Use equal groups, dot arrays, and area rectangles to understand why multiplication works.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/multipli.start: Build an array on the grid before trying mental-math shortcuts.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/multipli.check: Show why breaking a big rectangle into two smaller ones gives the exact same product.

lessons/mathematics/foundations/division.goal: Picture division as fair sharing or making equal groups, and check answers with multiplication.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/division.start: Drag counters into equal groups and predict if any will be left over.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/division.check: How can you use multiplication to prove your division answer is right?

lessons/mathematics/foundations/pemdas.h.goal: Evaluate math expressions step by step in the order every mathematician agrees on.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/pemdas.h.start: Predict the answer first, then step through the expression funnel one operation at a time.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/pemdas.h.check: Why do parentheses change the answer even when the numbers stay the same?

lessons/mathematics/foundations/fraction.goal: See that a fraction, a decimal, and a percent can name the exact same amount.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/fraction.start: Slide the point on the number line and watch all three forms update together.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/fraction.prerequisite: Understanding fractions as equal parts of a whole.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/fraction.check: Why do 3/4, 0.75, and 75% all land on the exact same spot?

lessons/mathematics/foundations/proporti.goal: Use unit rates and scale factors to compare prices, recipes, maps, and percents.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/proporti.start: Adjust the ratio sliders and watch how the matching quantity scales with it.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/proporti.check: In a proportional relationship, what stays constant when both numbers grow?

lessons/mathematics/foundations/area-per.goal: Measure both the inside (area) and the border (perimeter) of shapes you build.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/area-per.start: Click squares on the grid to build a shape and compare its area and perimeter.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/area-per.prerequisite: Counting squares and measuring side lengths.
lessons/mathematics/foundations/area-per.check: Can two shapes have the exact same perimeter but different areas?

lessons/mathematics/algebra/linear-equat.goal: Connect steady change to slope (m) and starting value (b) in y = mx + b.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/linear-equat.start: Predict how a line will tilt, then drag the two points to test your prediction.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/linear-equat.prerequisite: Plotting coordinates and working with negative numbers.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/linear-equat.check: What do the slope and the y-intercept each tell you in a real-world story?

lessons/mathematics/algebra/where-lines-.goal: Solve two equations together by finding the point where their lines cross.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/where-lines-.start: Move the two lines until they cross, run parallel, or overlap completely.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/where-lines-.prerequisite: Graphing lines and solving one-variable equations.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/where-lines-.check: How can you check that an intersection point works in both equations?

lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.goal: Turn any equation into a graph and test how changing one number shifts or bends the curve.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.start: Plot a function, change one parameter, and watch what moves on the grid.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.check: Which change in the equation caused the shift or stretch you saw on the graph?

lessons/mathematics/algebra/exponent-exp.goal: Compare steady adding against repeated multiplying and see why exponent rules work.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/exponent-exp.start: Compare the linear and exponential growth tracks step by step.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/exponent-exp.check: What grows by adding the same amount each step, and what grows by multiplying?

lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.goal: See why the squares on the two shorter sides of a right triangle equal the square on the longest side.
lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.start: Resize the right triangle and compare the areas of the three squares.
lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.check: Why does a² + b² = c² only hold true when there is a 90° angle?

lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.goal: Measure how circumference always stays π times bigger than diameter, no matter the circle's size.
lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.start: Roll the circle and compare the unrolled border to its diameter.
lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.check: When a circle doubles in diameter, what happens to its circumference and its area?

lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.goal: Pick the best measure of center (mean, median, or mode) and see how outliers affect it.
lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.start: Drag dots on the number line and watch the balance point (mean) and middle value (median) move.
lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.check: When one extreme number is added, which average changes most and why?

lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.goal: Measure how tightly or widely data values are clustered using range, IQR, and standard deviation.
lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.start: Build two datasets with the same mean, then drag points apart to watch the spread grow.
lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.check: What important story does a dataset's spread reveal that the average alone hides?

lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.goal: Compare what you expect to happen by chance with what actually happens over many trials.
lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.start: Predict the outcome, run 10 flips, then run 1,000 flips and compare.
lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.check: Why can 10 coin flips look uneven while 1,000 flips settle close to 50%?

lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.goal: Watch how many small left-or-right bounces stack up into a predictable bell curve.
lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.start: Predict which bin will catch the most balls before dropping them.
lessons/mathematics/statistics-and-proba.check: Why do so many balls end up near the middle bins instead of the far edges?

lessons/mathematics/algebra/algebra-tile.goal: Use rectangle area models to multiply expressions and factor quadratics back into pieces.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/algebra-tile.start: Arrange the x², x, and unit tiles until they form a solid rectangle.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/algebra-tile.check: How do the height and width of your rectangle match the factored answer?

lessons/mathematics/algebra/completing-t.goal: Turn a quadratic into a neat square by finding and adding the one missing corner piece.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/completing-t.start: Add the missing corner tile in the visual square and check both sides stay equal.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/completing-t.check: Why must you add the same corner value to both sides of the equation?

lessons/mathematics/algebra/logarithm-sc.goal: Use logarithms as inverse exponents to ask 'What power got us here?' and compare huge scales.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/logarithm-sc.start: Pick a base and slide the target value to watch the exponent machine solve for the power.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/logarithm-sc.check: Why does a logarithmic scale show both whispers and jet engines clearly on one ruler?

lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.goal: Sketch shapes, unfold 3D solids into flat 2D nets, and slice cross-sections to see where formulas come from.
lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.start: Choose a shape or 3D solid, make a prediction, and unfold its net to check the area.
lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.prerequisite: Area, perimeter, triangles, and circle formulas.
lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.check: How does unfolding a cylinder or cone into a flat shape prove its surface area formula?

lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.goal: Use sine, cosine, and tangent ratios to find missing sides and angles in right triangles.
lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.start: Pick your reference angle first, then label Opposite, Adjacent, and Hypotenuse.
lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.check: Why do Opposite and Adjacent swap names when you switch to the other acute angle?

lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.goal: See how moving around a circle traces out smooth sine and cosine waves over time.
lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.start: Drag the point around the circle and watch its height and width draw the waves.
lessons/mathematics/geometry-and-trigono.check: How does one full lap around the circle appear on the wave graph?

lessons/mathematics/algebra/matrix-trans.goal: See how four numbers in a 2×2 matrix rotate, stretch, or shear every point on a grid.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/matrix-trans.start: Drag the blue and orange basis arrows to bend the grid and watch the determinant update.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/matrix-trans.check: What does a negative determinant tell you happened to the grid?

lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.goal: Build a recursive pattern where each number is the sum of the two before it, and test nature claims.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.start: Generate the next terms in the sequence, then compare spiral counts in nature.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.check: What evidence actually confirms a Fibonacci spiral in a plant or shell?

lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.goal: Understand cube twists as reversible moves and see why move order changes the result.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.start: Run a short sequence of twists, then reverse it step by step.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.check: Why must you undo moves in reverse order to get back to where you started?

lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.goal: Rediscover the number e through continuous compounding and see why e^x equals its own slope.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.start: Compound interest faster and faster in the lab to watch the total approach e.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.prerequisite: Exponents, logarithms, and rates of growth.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.check: Why does more frequent compounding level off at e instead of growing to infinity?

lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.goal: Zoom into a curved graph until it looks straight and find its exact slope at a single point.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.start: Zoom in on the curve and watch secant lines settle onto the tangent line.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.prerequisite: Slope of a line and functions.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.check: What happens to the average slope between two points as they get infinitely close?

lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.goal: Climb from position to speed, acceleration, jerk, and snap to see how derivatives measure change.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.start: Change the motion profile and inspect how each curve on the derivative ladder responds.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.prerequisite: Slope of a curve and motion graphs.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.check: Why do elevator and roller-coaster engineers limit jerk as well as acceleration?

lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.goal: Build hills from layered waves and use slope (gradient) to predict which way water flows.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.start: Adjust the terrain waves and drop water to watch it follow the steepest downhill path.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.prerequisite: Functions, sine waves, and slope of a curve.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.check: How does the terrain's slope determine both the direction and speed of flowing water?

lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.goal: Slice curved shapes into thin rectangles to compute exact area and connect integrals to derivatives.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.start: Increase the number of slices (N) and watch the total area settle on the exact integral.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.prerequisite: Slope of a curve and area of rectangles.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.check: Why is the slope of the accumulated-area graph always equal to the height of the original curve?

lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.goal: Build complex waves from simple sine waves and inspect sounds and images by frequency.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.start: Add harmonics one at a time in the wave builder and watch the square wave appear.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.prerequisite: Sine waves, graphing functions, and area under a curve.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.check: What changes in a sound or shape when you add higher-frequency waves?

prereqLinks.title: Area Under a Curve: Accumulation & Integrals

lessons/mathematics/algebra/equations-ic.goal: Compare how equations model everything from shopping discounts to orbits and spacetime.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/equations-ic.start: Pick a depth layer on the iceberg and unpack what each symbol in the equation means.
lessons/mathematics/algebra/equations-ic.check: What real-world assumptions make your chosen equation work?

lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.goal: Explore how zeta zeros relate to prime numbers and compare examples with formal machine-checked proof.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.start: Inspect the complex-plane explorer and see where the zeta zeros line up.
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.prerequisite: Prime numbers, coordinates, and complex-plane ideas (optional extension).
lessons/mathematics/advanced-and-calculu.check: Why is checking billions of examples not enough for a mathematical proof?
